subject: Proposal: multi-wave tenor bridge + usage guardrails (draft term sheet)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie White <sophie.white@cleverlytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: multi-wave tenor bridge + usage guardrails (draft term sheet)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I outlined a draft that balances Cleverlytics' desire for predictable economics with flexibility for an aggressive onboarding ramp. High-level summary: 

- Term: 24-month committed capacity with a multi-wave ladder (Months 1-6: 50% of committed tokens available as base; Months 7-12: +25%; Months 13-24: full committed capacity)
- Usage floors: quarterly usage floors at 70% of committed monthly equivalent to protect pricing tiers; true-ups quarterly with pro-rated credits for overage/backfill
- Burst: an on-demand burst pool (up to 2.5x baseline) billed at a nominal premium; automatic fallback to burst when sustained 3-day average > 90% of capacity
- Co-terming: we’ll align to Cleverlytics' FY-end (Sep 30) with a short 3-month bridge to co-term for the first year
- Auto-renew: optional auto-renew at pre-agreed escalation (2% annual) unless opt-out 60 days prior

I've attached a draft term sheet (2026-08-23_CLV_term_sheet_draft.pdf) and a billing cadence matrix for reference.

Questions for you: preferred start date, any mandatory invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly), and whether procurement/legal want an initial redline window before we send to DocuSign.

If this looks directionally correct, I'll loop in Marissa for onboarding ops details and Karthik for commercial finalization.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side before we loop legal/procurement: 

1) Billing cadence: Cleverlytics prefers quarterly invoicing net 30, but we can consider monthly if there’s a strong technical reason.
2) Early exit: do you offer pro-rated credit if we accelerate adoption and want to convert to a usage-first model mid-term?
3) Burst billing: can burst be capped monthly to avoid surprise invoices? We prefer a soft cap and an alerting threshold at 75%.
4) SLA credits: what’s the credit framework if we experience latency or availability issues during ramp?

Procurement (cc) will propose available windows for contract review; please include a short ops checklist so our infra team can validate integration milestones.

— Sophie

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Sophie’s clarifying questions (excerpted below). Can you confirm feasibility and any operational guards we need to add to the term sheet? Attaching ops_onboarding_checklist.pdf and billing_cadence_matrix.xlsx.

Excerpt from Sophie: 
"Billing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoicing net 30 — can we get that? Early exit: pro-rated credit if we convert to usage-first mid-term? Burst billing: cap and alerting at 75%. SLA credits: framework during ramp?"

Specific asks: 
- Can we support quarterly invoicing for a committed 24-month? Any pricing uplift for quarter billing vs. monthly? (pricing team comp will decide)
- Do we have a standard addendum for converting committed spend to usage-first mid-term (with crediting rules)?
- Recommend a safe burst cap mechanism (e.g., burst allowance + alerting + manual opt-in for sustained overage) — is 2.5x acceptable operationally?
- SLA credit template — Marissa, can CS propose a 5% credit for any monthly downtime > 99.5% (examples welcome)

Timelines: Sophie is hoping to finalize terms and DocuSign next week if possible.

Thanks — Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-24T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: multi-wave tenor bridge + usage guardrails (ops + billing questions)

Ben / Karthik —

All feasible with these recommendations and constraints: 

1) Quarterly invoicing: operationally fine. Finance prefers a 1% billing cadence surcharge for quarterly vs. monthly to cover reconciliation. We can waive on strategic deals, but flag to pricing.

2) Early-exit conversion: we have a standard conversion addendum. Typical pattern: remaining committed balance converted to usage credit at a shortfall rate (70% of committed list), applied over next two quarters. We can tighten for Cleverlytics given ramp commitments.

3) Burst handling: propose the following safe-guard: 
   - Soft cap alert at 75% of baseline — alert to customer and Redwood ops
   - Automatic burst allowance up to 2x baseline for <= 72 hours (this prevents throttling during short spikes)
   - Sustained above-2x requires manual approval or pre-authorized overage pool; capped at 2.5x for invoicing purposes

4) SLA credits: CS recommends the standard SLA table (attached runbook link). For ramp period (first 90 days) reduce credit trigger to monthly availability < 99.0% => 5% credit; after ramp revert to 99.5% => 3% credit.

5) Onboarding / canary: Ops checklist attached. Recommend a 14-day pre-warm (canary) with telemetry validation gates: token throughput, p95 latency, and error rate. Full uplift scheduled in waves described by Ben.

I'll update the term sheet with the 1% quarterly surcharge as an optional line-item and include the conversion addendum summary. Karthik — please confirm pricing language for the surge premium and whether to offer a 6-month frontloaded credit to accelerate adoption.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Sophie / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Marissa/Karthik feedback we updated the draft:

- Quarterly invoicing: supported (optional 1% reconciliation surcharge; Redwood can waive on signature)
- Burst: soft-alert at 75%; automatic 2x allowance for <=72 hours; manual approval for sustained >2x; invoicing cap at 2.5x
- Early conversion addendum: remaining committed credit converts at 70% of list and applies over next two quarters (we can accelerate per negotiated clause)
- SLA credits: ramp window (first 90 days) has a 99.0% threshold -> 5% monthly credit; thereafter 99.5% -> 3% credit
- Start date: proposed Oct 1, 2026; onboarding canary window: Sep 20–Oct 4 (14 days pre-warm)

Next steps: I’ve attached the redline-ready term sheet and ops checklist (2026-08-23_CLV_term_sheet_draft.pdf, ops_onboarding_checklist.pdf). If procurement is good with quarterly net30 we can send to DocuSign (link below) for signature and schedule kickoff.
